metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - Moves past illness
metadata.description: Mo Alie-Cox (illness) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London.
metadata.analysis: Alie-Cox missed the Colts' first two practices of the week due to an illness, but he returned to the field Friday and avoided a designation heading into the weekend. He'll be ready to serve in his usual depth role at tight end behind starter Tyler Warren.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox (illness) cleared to play Sunday
metadata.description: Mo Alie-Cox (illness) has been cleared to play for Sunday morning's game against the Washington Commanders.
metadata.analysis: The Colts will have their veteran tight end on Sunday, as Alie-Cox has been cleared to play after missing two practices early in the week due to an illness. He remains off of the fantasy radar moving forward, however.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox (illness) absent from practice Thursday
metadata.description: Mo Alie-Cox (illness) was absent from Indianapolis' practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran is still recovering from an illness and didn't practice on Thursday as a result. It seems likely that he will play in Week 4, but we won't know for sure until closer to game time.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - Not practicing Thursday
metadata.description: Alie-Cox (illness) did not participate in practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Alie-Cox missed his second straight day of practice with an illness. It's unclear how long the 33-year-old will be absent from practice, but should he return Friday, there is a good chance he's available for Sunday's game in London. However, if Alie-Cox is unable to suit up, Drew Ogletree could see more tight-end reps behind Tyler Warren.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - Misses practice with illness
metadata.description: Alie-Cox (illness) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The nature of Alie-Cox's ailment is unknown, so it's not clear whether his availability for Week 4 is in any jeopardy. If he can return to practice Thursday or Friday, he'll put himself in a good position to suit up Sunday at Washington.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox (illness) misses practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Mo Alie-Cox (illness) missed Indianapolis' practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran tight end was unable to practice on Wednesday due to an illness. He's likely considered day-to-day for the time being, but there's a good chance that he'll be cleared to play in time for Sunday morning's game against the Washington Commanders.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox stays with Colts on one-year deal
metadata.description: Veteran tight end Mo Alie-Cox is staying with the Indianapolis Colts for another season as the two sides agreed on a one-year deal.
metadata.analysis: Alie-Cox has spent all eight of his seasons in the NFL with the Colts and has 127 career receptions for 1,550 yards and 16 touchdowns. Known more for his blocking ability, he did combine for 55 catches, 710 yards, and six scores in 2020 and 2021, but has not caught more than 19 passes in a season since. The Colts may look for a tight end in the upcoming draft, but Alie-Cox gives the team a veteran presence at the position. He's good for 10-15 catches and roughly 150 yards, but he's a player who is better in real life than in fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - Returning to Indy
metadata.description: Alie-Cox is re-signing with the Colts on a one-year contract, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
metadata.analysis: Alie-Cox has spent the first eight campaigns of his career in Indianapolis and hasn't missed a regular-season game since 2020. While he hasn't topped 189 regular-season receiving yards since 2021, the veteran tight end has been useful in the red zone, with 12 of his 81 catches going for touchdowns over the past five campaigns. Tyler Warren is firmly established as Indianapolis' long-term starter at the position, but Alie-Cox's return gives the Colts veteran leadership and elite run blocking at tight end.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox Re-Signing with Colts
metadata.description: Veteran tight end Mo Alie-Cox has agreed to a one-year deal that will keep him with the Indianapolis Colts for his 10th season in 2026. At 6-foot-5 and 267 pounds, Alie-Cox is a red-zone threat that must be accounted for, as evidenced by his 16 career touchdowns, but his most notable contribution is as one of the premier run-blocking tight ends in the league. Three-time Pro-Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor has topped 1,400 rushing yards and double-digit touchdowns in back-to-back seasons, and if the recently re-signed Daniel Jones can return to form following a season-ending Achilles injury, Taylor is a legitimate threat for the second rushing title of his career.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - Stays involved in season finale
metadata.description: Alie-Cox secured three of four targets for 22 yards during Sunday's 38-30 season-finale loss to Houston.
metadata.analysis: Alie-Cox didn't log a single appearance with more than one catch across the first 14 games of the 2025 campaign, but he compiled two, three and three catches in Indianapolis' final three contests, with one touchdown in that span. He wraps the season with a 13-117-1 receiving line on 20 targets, while having suited up for all 17 regular-season games and handling a depth role behind rookie standout Tyler Warren. Alie-Cox, who has spent all eight seasons of his NFL career so far with the Colts, will be an unrestricted free agent this offseason.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - Nabs touchdown vs. Jags
metadata.description: Alie-Cox caught all three of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Through the Colts' first 14 games this season, Alie-Cox had caught just five of 11 targets for 59 yards. However, in the team's last two games, the VCU product has secured all five of his targets for 36 yards and a touchdown, suggesting his role in Indianapolis' offense may be expanding. He's expected to operate as the Colts' No. 2 tight end in the Week 18 matchup against the Texans.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox catches touchdown Sunday
metadata.description: Mo Alie-Cox caught 3-of-3 targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Colts 23-17 loss against the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Alie-Cox caught the lone touchdown thrown by Philip Rivers. It was his first touchdown of the season.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - Two catches against San Francisco
metadata.description: Alie-Cox caught both of his targets for 16 yards in Monday's 48-27 loss to the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: Alie-Cox continued his depth role at tight end Monday, playing just 13 of the Colts' 60 offensive snaps behind rookie Tyler Warren (53). The veteran's two grabs were his first catches since Week 12, bring him to seven receptions for 75 yards on the season. Barring an injury to Warren, Alie-Cox remains far off the fantasy radar as the Colts prepare to host the Jaguars in Week 17.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - No catches in Week 8
metadata.description: Alie-Cox didn't draw a target while playing 16 of the Colts' 53 snaps on offense in Sunday's 38-14 win over the Titans.
metadata.analysis: The big-bodied Alie-Cox has taken the field for at least 30 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Colts' first eight games, but he continues to be utilized mainly as a blocker while standout rookie Tyler Warren functions as the top pass-catching option at the position. With four receptions for 50 yards on six targets this season, Alie-Cox isn't a total non-entity in the passing game, but he's not earning enough volume to put himself on the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox - One reception in season opener
metadata.description: Alie-Cox had one reception for 20 yards on his only target in Sunday's win over Miami.
metadata.analysis: Alie-Cox was the clear No. 2 tight end after Tyler Warren as he played on 33 of the offense's 73 snaps . Warren played 53 snaps and Andrew Ogletree played 27 snaps. Alie-Cox is mostly a blocking tight end and his profile in the passing game will be minimal with Warren taking over as the primary tight end.

metadata.title: Mo Alie-Cox Remaining With Colts
metadata.description: The Indianapolis Colts have re-signed tight end Mo Alie-Cox to a one-year deal on Friday. Alie-Cox is headed back to Indy for a eighth straight season. In 2024, Alie-Cox finished with 12 receptions for 147 yards and one touchdown in 17 games (13 starts) with the Colts. At this point, Alie-Cox is mainly depth as the Colts are likely to target a tight end during the upcoming NFL Draft. Regardless, it's hard to imagine Alie-Cox having fantasy value considering he hasn't posted a season with over 200 receiving yards since 2021. This appears to be a depth signing as Alie-Cox knows the system and the organization well.
